fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled configuration bytes are installed as the lexer scan region [pos, end); pos advances through the raw input while the lexer looks for tokens and string terminators.
When the input begins with three single quotes, lex_config routes control into lex_multiline_string, which then scans forward looking for the closing ''' string terminator.
lexer->pos is advanced past the opening delimiter; the do/while loop below then probes 3 bytes at a time for the closing ''' terminator, advancing one byte per iteration.

Root cause: strncmp() reads 3 bytes at lexer->pos while looking for the string terminator without first checking that at least 3 characters remain (the fix adds 'if (remaining(lexer) < 3) break;'). With an unterminated multiline string, pos advances to end-1 and the 3-byte probe crosses past lexer->end.

Sink: the unchecked strncmp() performs the out-of-bounds read. For a full 32768-byte fuzz input ('\''\''\'' followed by non-terminator bytes), the final probe at pos = end-1 reads bytes at indices size-2, size-1 and size, i.e. one byte past the intended 32768-byte buffer.

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: lwan-config.c lex_multiline_string() probes strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3) for the '''/""" string terminator without checking that at least 3 characters remain in the buffer, so an unterminated multiline string makes the loop read past the end of the config buffer; fixed upstream by 'Ensure there's enough characters while looking for string terminator' which adds a remaining(lexer) < 3 check.
